items.q: What is the recommended maximum daily dose of paracetamol (acetaminophen) for a healthy adult, in grams? Give the range.

source.title: Paracetamol
source.quote: at a recommended maximum daily dose for an adult of three to four grams

items.q: Which antidote is given for paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?
choices: Acetylcysteine
Naloxone
Flumazenil
Vitamin K

key.answer: Acetylcysteine

source.title: Paracetamol poisoning
source.quote: If there is a potential for toxicity, the antidote acetylcysteine is recommended.

items.q: High doses of aspirin may cause which symptom?
choices: Ringing in the ears
Blue-tinted vision
Hair loss
Yellow teeth

key.answer: Ringing in the ears

source.title: Aspirin
source.quote: High doses may result in ringing in the ears.

items.q: Why are antibiotics useless against the common cold and influenza?
choices: Those illnesses are caused by viruses, and antibiotics do not work on viruses
Colds and flu are caused by fungi
Antibiotics only work on illnesses that cause fever
The doses sold are too low to matter

key.answer: Those illnesses are caused by viruses, and antibiotics do not work on viruses

source.title: Antibiotic
source.quote: Antibiotics are not effective against viruses such as the ones which cause the common cold or influenza.

items.q: What should a burn be cooled with?
choices: Cool water at 10-25 °C (50-77 °F), not ice water
Ice water, to cool it as fast as possible
Butter or oil
Water heated to 40 °C (104 °F)

key.answer: Cool water at 10-25 °C (50-77 °F), not ice water

source.title: Burn
source.quote: It should be performed with cool water 10-25 °C (50.0-77.0 °F) and not ice water as the latter can cause further injury.

items.q: Above what blood alcohol concentration, in percent, may levels be fatal?

source.title: Blood alcohol content
source.quote: Levels above 0.40% (4 g/L ) may be fatal.

items.q: Why does alcohol dehydrate you?
choices: It increases urine production (diuresis)
It blocks the kidneys from making urine
It evaporates water through the skin
It destroys red blood cells

key.answer: It increases urine production (diuresis)

source.title: Hangover
source.quote: Ethanol has a dehydrating effect by causing increased urine production (diuresis)

items.q: At what rate per minute should adult chest compressions be given in CPR? Give the range.

source.title: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
source.quote: at a rate of at least 100 to 120 per minute

items.q: How deep should adult chest compressions in CPR be, in centimetres? Give the range.

source.title: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
source.quote: chest compressions for adults between 5 cm (2.0 in) and 6 cm (2.4 in) deep

items.q: Heat stroke is defined by a body temperature greater than what value, in degrees Celsius?

source.title: Heat stroke
source.quote: a severe heat illness that results in a body temperature greater than 40.0 °C (104.0 °F)

items.q: After the initial tetanus vaccine doses, how often are additional doses recommended to maintain immunity, in years?

source.title: Tetanus vaccine
source.quote: additional doses every ten years are recommended to maintain immunity

items.q: After an injury, a tetanus booster should be given within how many hours for someone whose immunisation is out of date?

source.title: Tetanus vaccine
source.quote: A booster shot should be given within 48 hours of an injury to people whose immunization is out of date.

items.q: A rash that does not fade when a glass is rolled over it may accompany which serious infection?
choices: Meningitis
Eczema
Hay fever
Sunburn

key.answer: Meningitis

source.title: Meningitis
source.quote: A non-blanching rash (a rash that does not fade when a glass is rolled over it) may also be present.

items.q: In the stroke warning mnemonic FAST, what does the T stand for?
choices: Time to call emergency services
Tremor
Temperature
Tingling

key.answer: Time to call emergency services

source.title: Stroke
source.quote: FAST (facial droop, arm weakness, speech difficulty, and time to call emergency services)

items.q: Which drug, injected into the outer thigh muscle, is the primary treatment for anaphylaxis? (one word)

key.answer: epinephrine

source.title: Anaphylaxis
source.quote: Epinephrine (adrenaline) (1:1000) is the primary treatment for anaphylaxis with no absolute contraindication to its use.

items.q: After anaphylaxis symptoms resolve, hospital observation is recommended for how many hours, because of biphasic anaphylaxis? Give the range.

source.title: Anaphylaxis
source.quote: in-hospital observation for between 2 and 24 hours is recommended for people once they have returned to normal due to concerns of biphasic anaphylaxis

items.q: Which three findings make up the quick SOFA (qSOFA) sepsis screen, of which at least two are needed?
choices: Increased breathing rate, change in level of consciousness, low blood pressure
High fever, rash, joint pain
Low heart rate, high blood sugar, blurred vision
Cough, sore throat, runny nose

key.answer: Increased breathing rate, change in level of consciousness, low blood pressure

source.title: Sepsis
source.quote: qSOFA criteria for sepsis include at least two of the following three: increased breathing rate, change in the level of consciousness, and low blood pressure

items.q: Hypothermia is diagnosed at a body temperature below what value, in degrees Celsius?

source.title: Hypothermia
source.quote: body temperature below 35.0 °C (95.0 °F)

items.q: In the United States, what does the Miranda warning advise a suspect in police custody of?
choices: Their right to silence and protection from self-incrimination
Their right to leave at any time
Their right to have charges dropped after 24 hours
Their right to refuse fingerprinting

key.answer: Their right to silence and protection from self-incrimination

source.title: Miranda warning
source.quote: advising them of their right to silence and, in effect, protection from self-incrimination

items.q: In what year did the U.S. Supreme Court decide Miranda v. Arizona?

source.title: Miranda warning
source.quote: Named for the U.S. Supreme Court's 1966 decision Miranda v. Arizona

items.q: Under the Fifth Amendment of the US Constitution, what does the Double Jeopardy Clause give a defendant?
choices: The right to be tried only once for the same offense
The right to a trial by a jury of peers
The right to refuse any police search
The right to a speedy trial

key.answer: The right to be tried only once for the same offense

source.title: Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution
source.quote: provides the right of defendants to be tried only once in federal court for the same offense

items.q: In the United States, "pleading the Fifth" is used to invoke which protection?
choices: The Self-Incrimination Clause, to decline answers that might incriminate you
The Double Jeopardy Clause, to stop a second trial
The Takings Clause, to protect property
The Due Process Clause, to demand a lawyer be paid for

key.answer: The Self-Incrimination Clause, to decline answers that might incriminate you

source.title: Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution
source.quote: is a colloquial term often used to invoke the Self-Incrimination Clause when witnesses decline to answer questions where the answers might incriminate them

items.q: In common-law jurisdictions such as the United States, what happens to the estate of a person who dies without a legally valid will?
choices: It is distributed under statutory intestacy laws, typically favouring close relatives
It passes automatically to the state treasury
It goes to the eldest sibling alone
It stays frozen until a court finds a will

key.answer: It is distributed under statutory intestacy laws, typically favouring close relatives

source.title: Intestacy
source.quote: Intestacy is the condition of the estate of a person who dies without a legally valid will, resulting in the distribution of their estate under statutory intestacy laws rather than by their expressed wishes

items.q: In a US criminal trial, what is jury nullification?
choices: A not-guilty verdict even though the jury believes the defendant broke the law
A verdict thrown out because a juror was dismissed
A judge overruling a guilty verdict
A guilty verdict reached without unanimity

key.answer: A not-guilty verdict even though the jury believes the defendant broke the law

source.title: Jury nullification
source.quote: is a decision by the jury in a criminal trial resulting in a verdict of not guilty even though they believe a defendant has broken the law

items.q: In US jurisdictions that have a duty to retreat, what does it require?
choices: That a threatened person retreat to a place of safety, if possible, before using lethal force in self-defense
That police be called before any use of force
That the person fire a warning first
That the person leave the state

key.answer: That a threatened person retreat to a place of safety, if possible, before using lethal force in self-defense

source.title: Duty to retreat
source.quote: a legal requirement in some jurisdictions that a threatened person cannot harm another in self-defense (especially lethal force) when it is possible instead to retreat to a place of safety

items.q: What does a statute of limitations set?
choices: The maximum time after an event within which legal proceedings may be started
The minimum sentence for an offence
The maximum fine a court may impose
The number of appeals allowed

key.answer: The maximum time after an event within which legal proceedings may be started

source.title: Statute of limitations
source.quote: a law passed by a legislative body to set the maximum time after an event within which legal proceedings may be initiated

items.q: Under Terry v. Ohio in the United States, police may briefly stop and detain a person based on:
choices: Reasonable suspicion of involvement in a crime
An unexplained hunch alone
Proof beyond a reasonable doubt
A signed arrest warrant

key.answer: Reasonable suspicion of involvement in a crime

source.title: Reasonable suspicion
source.quote: a person can be stopped and briefly detained by a police officer based on a reasonable suspicion of involvement in a punishable crime

items.q: In US criminal law, probable cause is the standard police need to obtain what?
choices: An arrest warrant or search warrant
A Miranda waiver
A jury summons
A bail reduction

key.answer: An arrest warrant or search warrant

source.title: Probable cause
source.quote: probable cause is the legal standard by which police authorities have reason to obtain a warrant for the arrest of a suspected criminal and for a court's issuing of a search warrant

items.q: Which of these is one of the four factors a US court weighs in deciding fair use?
choices: The purpose and character of the use, including whether it is commercial or nonprofit educational
Whether the author is still alive
Whether the work was first published abroad
Whether a copyright notice appeared on the work

key.answer: The purpose and character of the use, including whether it is commercial or nonprofit educational

source.title: Fair use
source.quote: the purpose and character of the use, including whether such use is of a commercial nature or is for nonprofit educational purposes; the nature of the copyrighted work; the amount and substantiality of the portion used

items.q: Under a power of attorney, what is the person authorised to act for the grantor called? (one word)

key.answer: agent

source.title: Power of attorney
source.quote: The one authorized to act is the agent

items.q: In the United States, what does at-will employment let an employer do?
choices: Dismiss an employee for any reason, without warning, as long as the reason is not illegal
Dismiss an employee only after three written warnings
Dismiss an employee only for proven misconduct
Dismiss an employee only with severance pay

key.answer: Dismiss an employee for any reason, without warning, as long as the reason is not illegal

source.title: At-will employment
source.quote: an employer's ability to dismiss an employee for any reason (that is, without having to establish "just cause" for termination), and without warning

items.q: In most of the world, the default copyright term is the life of the author plus how many years? Give the range.

source.title: Copyright
source.quote: In most of the world, the default length of copyright is the life of the author plus either 50 or 70 years.

items.q: In the United States, what does the castle doctrine protect?
choices: Using force, up to deadly force, against an intruder in your home free from prosecution
A landlord's right to enter without notice
A tenant's right to withhold rent
A homeowner's right to keep trespassers' belongings

key.answer: Using force, up to deadly force, against an intruder in your home free from prosecution

source.title: Castle doctrine
source.quote: designates a person's abode or any legally occupied place (for example, an automobile or a home) as a place in which that person has protections and immunities permitting one, in certain circumstances, to use force

items.q: In the United States, what does the exclusionary rule do?
choices: Prevents evidence collected in violation of a defendant's constitutional rights from being used in court
Excludes jurors with a criminal record
Bars defendants from testifying
Excludes expert witnesses from a trial

key.answer: Prevents evidence collected in violation of a defendant's constitutional rights from being used in court

source.title: Exclusionary rule
source.quote: prevents evidence collected or analyzed in violation of the defendant's constitutional rights from being used in a court of law

items.q: What is the difference between APY and APR?
choices: APY is the rate paid to a depositor; APR is the rate paid by a borrower
APY applies only to credit cards; APR only to savings
APY ignores compounding; APR includes it
They are identical

key.answer: APY is the rate paid to a depositor; APR is the rate paid by a borrower

source.title: Annual percentage yield
source.quote: APY generally refers to the rate paid to a depositor by a financial institution, while the analogous annual percentage rate (APR) refers to the rate paid to a financial institution by a borrower.

items.q: The 4% rule for retirement withdrawals assumes the portfolio must last how many years?

source.title: Trinity study
source.quote: It is assumed that the portfolio needs to last thirty years.

items.q: What does academic research find about most active stock pickers compared with the index?
choices: They underperform the relevant index after fees and taxes
They beat the index most years
They match the index exactly
They outperform only in bull markets

key.answer: They underperform the relevant index after fees and taxes

source.title: Index fund
source.quote: Academic research has consistently found that most active investors (stock pickers) within a given market segment underperform the relevant index after fees and taxes.

items.q: What is a Ponzi scheme?
choices: A fraud that pays profits to earlier investors with funds from newer investors
A legal tax shelter for retirement savings
A loan that is repaid with future wages
An index fund that tracks a bond market

key.answer: A fraud that pays profits to earlier investors with funds from newer investors

source.title: Ponzi scheme
source.quote: a form of fraud that lures investors and pays profits to earlier investors with funds from more recent investors

items.q: What does Chapter 7 of the US bankruptcy code govern?
choices: Liquidation
Reorganization with a repayment plan
Farm debt restructuring only
Municipal debt adjustment

key.answer: Liquidation

source.title: Chapter 7, Title 11, United States Code
source.quote: Chapter 7 of Title 11 U.S. Code is the bankruptcy code that governs the process of liquidation under the bankruptcy laws of the United States.

items.q: How does compound interest differ from simple interest?
choices: Previously accumulated interest is added to the principal
Interest is charged only once a year
The rate is fixed by law
Interest is never added to the balance

key.answer: Previously accumulated interest is added to the principal

source.title: Compound interest
source.quote: Compound interest is contrasted with simple interest, where previously accumulated interest is not added to the principal amount of the current period.

items.q: Under the US Fair Credit Reporting Act, negative information is removed from a credit report how many years after the date of first delinquency?

source.title: Fair Credit Reporting Act
source.quote: Remove negative information seven years after the date of first delinquency

items.q: The FDIC insures deposits in member banks up to how many US dollars per ownership category? Answer with a number.

source.title: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
source.quote: the FDIC insures deposits in member banks up to $250,000 per ownership category

items.q: How is a Roth IRA taxed, compared with a traditional IRA?
choices: No tax deduction for contributions, but qualified withdrawals are tax-free
Contributions are deducted, and withdrawals are taxed
Both contributions and withdrawals are tax-free
Growth in the account is taxed every year

key.answer: No tax deduction for contributions, but qualified withdrawals are tax-free

source.title: Roth IRA
source.quote: rather than granting an income tax reduction for contributions to the retirement plan, qualified withdrawals from the Roth IRA plan are tax-free, and growth in the account is tax-free

items.q: In the FICO credit score, payment history makes up what percentage of the score?

source.title: Credit score in the United States
source.quote: Payment history (35%): Best described as the presence or lack of derogatory information.

items.q: A US Chapter 13 bankruptcy repayment plan usually runs for how many years? Give the range.

source.title: Chapter 13, Title 11, United States Code
source.quote: Chapter 13 plans are usually three to five years in length and may not exceed five years.

items.q: What is a fund's expense ratio?
choices: The total percentage of fund assets used for administrative, management, advertising and other expenses
The yearly percentage return of the fund
The share of the fund held in cash
The fee charged only when you sell

key.answer: The total percentage of fund assets used for administrative, management, advertising and other expenses

source.title: Expense ratio
source.quote: The expense ratio of a stock or asset fund is the total percentage of fund assets used for administrative, management, advertising (12b-1), and all other expenses.

items.q: Payday lenders charging the maximum the law allows can reach an annual percentage rate as high as what percent?

source.title: Payday loan
source.quote: which can be as high as 400% annual percentage rate (APR)

items.q: What does inflation do to money?
choices: Reduces its purchasing power
Increases its purchasing power
Leaves its purchasing power unchanged
Raises interest earned on cash

key.answer: Reduces its purchasing power

source.title: Inflation
source.quote: inflation corresponds to a reduction in the purchasing power of money

items.q: Flumazenil is primarily used to treat overdose of which drug class?
choices: Benzodiazepines
Opioids
Stimulants
Paracetamol

key.answer: Benzodiazepines

source.title: Flumazenil
source.quote: Intravenous flumazenil is primarily used to treat benzodiazepine overdoses and to help reverse anesthesia.

items.q: Disulfiram makes drinking alcohol miserable because it causes a buildup of which compound?
choices: Acetaldehyde
Acetic acid
Methanol
Lactic acid

key.answer: Acetaldehyde

source.title: Disulfiram
source.quote: When the dehydrogenase enzyme is inhibited, acetaldehyde builds up, causing unpleasant side effects.

items.q: The European Food Safety Authority says up to how many milligrams of caffeine per day does not raise safety concerns for non-pregnant adults?

source.title: Caffeine
source.quote: up to 400 mg of caffeine per day (around 5.7 mg/kg of body mass per day) does not raise safety concerns for non-pregnant adults

items.q: Alcohol withdrawal usually begins how many hours after the last drink?

source.title: Alcohol withdrawal syndrome
source.quote: Usual onset Six hours following the last drink

items.q: What typically causes death in a barbiturate overdose?
choices: A lack of breathing
Liver failure
Kidney failure
A stroke

key.answer: A lack of breathing

source.title: Barbiturate overdose
source.quote: If death occurs, it is typically due to a lack of breathing.

items.q: Methadone's elimination half-life is how many hours? Give the range.

source.title: Methadone
source.quote: Elimination half-life 15-55 hours

items.q: Why can grapefruit juice raise the blood levels of many medications?
choices: It inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme that metabolizes them
It speeds up the kidneys' removal of drugs
It blocks absorption in the gut
It destroys the active ingredient in the stomach

key.answer: It inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme that metabolizes them

source.title: Grapefruit
source.quote: Furanocoumarins inhibit the CYP3A4 enzyme (among others from the cytochrome P450 enzyme family responsible for metabolizing 90% of drugs).

items.q: Naloxone blocks the effects of opioids for how many minutes? Give the range.

source.title: Naloxone
source.quote: Naloxone blocks the effects of opioids for 30 to 90 minutes.

items.q: How much alcohol is enough to almost completely saturate the liver's capacity to metabolize it?
choices: One standard drink
Three standard drinks
Six standard drinks
Ten standard drinks

key.answer: One standard drink

source.title: Alcohol (drug)
source.quote: One standard drink is sufficient to almost completely saturate the liver's capacity to metabolize alcohol.

items.q: After a dose of LSD, tolerance develops after how many hours?

source.title: LSD
source.quote: LSD shows significant tachyphylaxis, with tolerance developing 24 hours after administration.

items.q: How quickly does tolerance to psilocybin build and dissipate?
choices: Quickly, over days
Slowly, over months
It builds but never dissipates
No tolerance develops

key.answer: Quickly, over days

source.title: Psilocybin
source.quote: Tolerance to psilocybin builds and dissipates quickly

items.q: Nicotine's elimination half-life is how many hours? Give the range.

source.title: Nicotine
source.quote: Elimination half-life 1-2 hours
